I don't know — no number is committed. Nothing in writing exists yet: Marcus reports that Corvane's RM "hinted they want to raise the per-item fee after the Nov 10 reject mess," with "nothing on paper yet," and the renewal call slipped to the week of Nov 23 [6].

What the company has on record: the current agreement runs until March 31, 2027, and the planning assumption is that the Corvane per-item ACH fee stays at $0.08 in 2027 (revisit the bottom tier if it goes above $0.10) [1]. Note this is a per-item ACH fee, not a percentage of payout volume [1]. Marcus also stresses this only hits Quillon's margin, not customer pricing [1][6].
